name: Calculating the Winning Percentage of a Sports Team (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that receives from the user the number of games in a tournament and the number of the games that a sports team won in the tournament, and calculates the winning percentage of that sports team. The program must ask the user for each of the two inputs until the user enters a valid number.
code:
#Step 1: Read the number of games in the tournament
text = input("Enter the number of games in the tournament: ")
total_games = int(text)       
#Step 2: Validate the user input for the number of games in the tournament, ask for a valid input as long as the user enters an invalid number; otherwise stop
while total_games <= 0 :
    text = input("Enter the number of games in the tournament: ")
    total_games = int(text)
#Step 3: Read the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament
text = input("Enter the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament: ")
wins = int(text)      
#Step 4: Validate the user input for the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament, ask for a valid input as long as the user enters an invalid number; otherwise stop
while wins < 0 or wins > total_games :
    text = input("Enter the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament: ")
    wins = int(text)
#Step 5: Calculate and print the percentage of games won by a team
ratio = wins / total_games
print("Winning percentage:", ratio)

Best practices: Use a more descriptive name (e.g., games_str or user_input), consider calling .strip() to remove extra spaces, and handle conversion errors by checking the string or using try/except around int() so you can re-prompt the user instead of crashing. What it does not do: this line only collects a string — it does not convert the answer to an integer. The actual conversion happens on the next line (total_games = int(text)), so don’t assume text is a number yet.

Possible errors and misconceptions: if the user types something that is not an integer (letters, decimals, empty text), the conversion on the next line will raise an error and the program will crash. Also, if the user keeps entering invalid values, the loop will keep repeating.

Best practices you can apply: make the prompt explicit (for example: "Enter the number of games (positive integer): "), and handle bad input before converting — e.g. strip the text and use a try/except around int(text) or check characters first — so the program can give a clear error message instead of crashing.
User experience tip: consider printing a short message before re-prompting (like "Invalid input — please enter a positive integer") so the user understands why they are being asked again.
